stories.headline: Finland's drone threat response: government roundtable, household safety guide, warning system overhaul, and suspected Russian airspace violation
stories.summary: Following a drone alert that prompted 1.8 million Helsinki-region residents to shelter in place, PM Orpo hosted a cross-sector roundtable at Säätytalo on drone preparedness, announced plans for a practical household drone-safety booklet, and outlined three priority improvements to the public warning system including pay rules for workers unable to reach work during alerts. Defence Minister Häkkänen separately confirmed a suspected Russian military aircraft airspace violation over the Gulf of Finland on 27 May, and President Stubb stated from Rovaniemi that he does not believe Russia is deliberately directing drones toward Finland.

stories.headline: Orpo's IS interview and Yle interview hour signal fiscal and electoral positioning ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: In back-to-back major media appearances — an Ilta-Sanomat interview and the Yle Prime Minister interview hour — PM Orpo signalled willingness to review the pension system next term, dismissed SDP's austerity list as weak, said he is ready to form a government if Lindtman fails, and told Yle the economy is turning around. He also indicated no obstacle to releasing the long-secret 'Tiitinen list' of suspected Stasi informants, a statement that drew immediate public attention.

stories.headline: President Stubb's Rovaniemi visit and Hornet fighter flight draw international media attention
stories.summary: President Alexander Stubb made a two-day official visit to Rovaniemi, including an inspection of the Lapland Air Command where he flew in an F/A-18 Hornet fighter jet for the first time. Stubb emphasised Lapland's strategic importance to NATO's Arctic defence, and video and images from the flight went viral internationally, drawing reactions from foreign media and public figures.

Separately, Foreign Minister Valtonen told EU foreign ministers that Stubb would be an excellent candidate for a joint European negotiator role on Ukraine, a proposal drawing interest in international media.

stories.headline: Parliament fiscal debate: government defends corporate tax cut against SDP opposition as deficit projections loom
stories.summary: Finance Minister Purra and the SDP clashed sharply in parliament over the government's planned corporate tax cut and fiscal trajectory, with Purra defending the measure and attacking the opposition's counter-proposals as internally inconsistent. SDP demanded the corporate tax cut be reversed, while analysts offered mixed assessments. The debate was framed by EU Commission guidance that Finland must address its excessive deficit.

stories.headline: EK proposal to cut Sunday and overtime pay triggers cross-party backlash, Orpo rules it out
stories.summary: The Confederation of Finnish Industries (EK) called for cuts to statutory Sunday and overtime supplements, prompting PM Orpo to publicly rule out any such reform ('would never cross my mind'), while SDP demanded a joint cross-party commitment to protect the supplements. The issue became a focal point in pre-election partisan positioning.

Reports late in the week indicated the two parties reached a compromise.

stories.headline: Finland approves 33rd Ukraine military aid package worth €128 million
stories.summary: President Stubb, acting on a government proposal, signed off on Finland's 33rd military aid package to Ukraine valued at approximately €128 million, bringing the cumulative total to around €3.4 billion. Defence Minister Häkkänen noted the package also strengthens Finland's own defence-industrial base, as dozens of Finnish companies have supplied equipment through the support packages.

stories.headline: Civil society organisations demand Defence Minister Häkkänen resign over undisclosed Israel defence conference
stories.summary: A group of Finnish civil society organisations called on Defence Minister Häkkänen to resign, citing a Finland-Israel joint defence industry conference held in Helsinki in May that was organised without public announcement. Critics accused the ministry of inadequate transparency and said Häkkänen was unsuitable given Israel's conduct. Kokoomus youth organisations defended Häkkänen, saying he did nothing wrong.

stories.headline: SDP holds 48th party congress in Tampere, elects new leadership bodies
stories.summary: The Social Democratic Party concluded its 48th party congress in Tampere, electing new party council and party board members for 2026–2028. Emilia Kangaskolkka was elected party council chair, and the congress adopted an international resolution on Finland's foreign policy principles. The event drew attention to intra-party debate on the debt brake.

stories.headline: SUPO warns that Russia systematically uses Finland-based procurement networks to evade sanctions
stories.summary: Finland's Security Intelligence Service (SUPO) publicly warned that Russia is deliberately exploiting internationally linked networks operating in Finland to circumvent Western sanctions and supply its war industry. SUPO counterintelligence head Teemu Liikkanen said the networks existed before the 2022 invasion and use layered corporate structures to conceal Russian state connections.

stories.headline: Finland chairs OECD Ministerial Council Meeting in Paris; Orpo to meet Macron bilaterally
stories.summary: Finland will chair the OECD Ministerial Council Meeting in Paris on 3–4 June — its first time chairing the meeting in over 40 years. PM Orpo will open the meeting alongside Finance Minister Purra, Foreign Minister Valtonen, and others. Orpo will also hold a bilateral meeting with French President Macron on the sidelines.

stories.headline: POP Bank's 3-day total service outage over graduation weekend draws Consumer Union criticism
stories.summary: Finnish cooperative POP Bank shut down all digital banking services — online bank, mobile bank, and debit card payments — for approximately three days from 29 May to 1 June for a system upgrade, coinciding with Finland's graduation weekend. The Consumer Union called the timing 'particularly problematic', questioned liability rules, and the banking industry association defended planned outages as necessary for security upgrades.

stories.summary: Helsingin Sanomat reported that Länsi-Uusimaa police proposed lower-than-actual income figures when calculating SDP MP Joona Räsänen's day-fine for a drink-driving offence admitted in April. Follow-up reporting clarified police do not suspect Räsänen of deliberate fraud; the lower income figure appears to have been a police error. Räsänen had already said he would not seek re-election to SDP party bodies.
